title: Gather Django status strings into TextChoices
summary: Define a status that drifted between spellings once with models.TextChoices and choices=, then return its label with get_status_display().

files.content:
from django.db import models


class Order(models.Model):
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="pending")
    total = models.PositiveIntegerField()
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

turns.user: order status is a plain string and the db has both canceled and cancelled in it. counts were off. whats the right fix

assistant.body: Short answer: define the states once as a models.TextChoices class on the model and pass it to the CharField with choices=. That class becomes the single source of truth for the spelling. Code refers to Order.Status.CANCELLED, so a typo is an AttributeError instead of a silent new status. Note: save() does not check choices. Only forms and full_clean() reject an unknown value. The rows already stored as canceled get fixed with one update.

from django.db import models


class Order(models.Model):
    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        PENDING = "pending", "Pending"
        PAID = "paid", "Paid"
        SHIPPED = "shipped", "Shipped"
        CANCELLED = "cancelled", "Cancelled"

    status = models.CharField(
        max_length=20,
        choices=Status,
        default=Status.PENDING,
    )
    total = models.PositiveIntegerField()
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
python manage.py shell -c "from orders.models import Order; Order.objects.filter(status='canceled').update(status=Order.Status.CANCELLED)"

turns.user: migrated. also return the display name from the API, i want to kill the lookup table in the frontend

assistant.body: Sure thing. Django gives every field with choices a get_status_display() method. It returns the label for the stored value, so the mapping lives in one place on the model. The count also stops using a raw string and filters on Order.Status.CANCELLED.
